Under incomplete records, opening capital was ₦2,500,000 and closing capital was ₦3,600,000. Drawings were ₦400,000 while additional capital introduced was ₦300,000. The profit is
questions.explanation: Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital = ₦3.6m + ₦400k − ₦300k − ₦2.5m = ₦1.2m.

questions.text: Which of the following is a capital expenditure of government
questions.explanation: Construction of a hospital creates a long-term public asset and is therefore capital expenditure.

questions.text: The officer primarily responsible for keeping the financial records of the Federal Government and preparing its financial statements is the
questions.explanation: The Accountant-General is responsible for central government accounting and financial reporting functions.

questions.text: Which of the following is an important control in a computerized accounting system
options: Allowing unrestricted access to all accounting records
Segregating authorization, processing and review functions
questions.explanation: Segregation of duties reduces the risk of unauthorized transactions and fraud.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦8,000,000, opening inventory of ₦900,000, purchases of ₦4,500,000, closing inventory of ₦700,000 and operating expenses of ₦1,200,000. What is the operating profit
questions.explanation: Cost of sales = ₦900k + ₦4.5m − ₦700k = ₦4.7m. Gross profit = ₦8m − ₦4.7m = ₦3.3m. Operating profit = ₦3.3m − ₦1.2m = ₦2.1m.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦15,000,000, cost of sales of ₦9,000,000 and operating expenses of ₦2,500,000. What is the net profit margin
questions.explanation: Gross profit = ₦15m − ₦9m = ₦6m. Net profit = ₦6m − ₦2.5m = ₦3.5m. Net profit margin = ₦3.5m ÷ ₦15m × 100 = 23.33%.

questions.text: A machine costing ₦6,000,000 has a useful life of 8 years and a residual value of ₦600,000. Using the straight-line method, what is the net book value after 3 years
questions.explanation: Annual depreciation = (₦6m − ₦600k) ÷ 8 = ₦675,000. After 3 years, accumulated depreciation = ₦2.025m. NBV = ₦6m − ₦2.025m = ₦3.975m.

questions.text: A trader purchased goods worth ₦2,000,000 subject to a 15% trade discount and a further 5% cash discount for prompt payment. The amount recorded as purchases is
questions.explanation: Trade discount = 15% × ₦2m = ₦300,000. Net purchase = ₦2m − ₦300k = ₦1.7m. Cash discount is not deducted from purchases.

questions.text: A business has current assets of ₦6,500,000, current liabilities of ₦2,600,000, and inventory of ₦1,300,000. The acid-test ratio is
questions.explanation: Quick assets = ₦6.5m − ₦1.3m = ₦5.2m. Acid-test ratio = ₦5.2m ÷ ₦2.6m = 2.0:1.

questions.text: A company has issued 5,000,000 ordinary shares of ₦0.50 each. If the company declares a dividend of 8%, the dividend payable is
questions.explanation: Total nominal value = 5,000,000 × ₦0.50 = ₦2.5m. Dividend = 8% × ₦2.5m = ₦200,000.

questions.text: A manufacturing business has prime cost of ₦4,200,000 and factory overhead of ₦1,800,000. Opening work-in-progress was ₦500,000 and closing work-in-progress was ₦700,000. The cost of production is
questions.explanation: Production cost = Prime cost + Factory overhead + Opening WIP − Closing WIP = ₦4.2m + ₦1.8m + ₦500k − ₦700k = ₦5.8m.

questions.text: A partner withdraws goods costing ₦45,000 from the partnership for personal use. The accounting entry is
questions.explanation: Goods withdrawn by a partner are treated as drawings and reduce purchases/inventory.

questions.text: A club has subscriptions received in advance of ₦120,000 at the beginning of the year and ₦90,000 at the end. Subscriptions outstanding were ₦80,000 at the beginning and ₦110,000 at the end. If cash received during the year was ₦2,500,000, the subscription income is
questions.explanation: Income = Cash received + closing arrears − opening arrears + opening advance − closing advance = ₦2.5m + ₦110k − ₦80k + ₦120k − ₦90k = ₦2.56m.

questions.text: A business has opening capital of ₦5,000,000, closing capital of ₦6,200,000, drawings of ₦800,000 and additional capital of ₦400,000. The profit for the year is
questions.explanation: Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital = ₦6.2m + ₦800k − ₦400k − ₦5m = ₦1.6m.

questions.text: A trader has sales of ₦8,500,000 and a gross profit margin of 32%. What is the cost of sales
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 32% × ₦8.5m = ₦2.72m. Cost of sales = ₦8.5m − ₦2.72m = ₦5.78m.

questions.text: A business has current assets of ₦10,000,000 and current liabilities of ₦4,000,000. It purchases inventory worth ₦1,000,000 on credit. The new current ratio is
questions.explanation: New current assets = ₦11m. New current liabilities = ₦5m. Ratio = ₦11m ÷ ₦5m = 2.2:1.

questions.text: A machine costing ₦3,500,000 was depreciated at 15% per annum using the reducing-balance method. What is the accumulated depreciation after two years
questions.explanation: Year 1 depreciation = 15% × ₦3.5m = ₦525,000. NBV = ₦2.975m. Year 2 depreciation = 15% × ₦2.975m = ₦446,250. Accumulated depreciation = ₦525,000 + ₦446,250 = ₦971,250. None of the options matches exactly. DO NOT USE.

questions.text: A business has credit sales of ₦10,000,000. Opening receivables were ₦1,200,000 and closing receivables were ₦1,800,000. The receivables turnover is
questions.explanation: Average receivables = (₦1.2m + ₦1.8m) ÷ 2 = ₦1.5m. Receivables turnover = ₦10m ÷ ₦1.5m = 6.67 times.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of revenue expenditure
options: Cost of rebuilding a damaged warehouse
Repairs and maintenance of office equipment
Purchase of a new delivery vehicle
questions.explanation: Repairs and maintenance are revenue expenditure as they maintain existing assets rather than improving them.

questions.text: A manufacturing business has direct materials of ₦2,500,000, direct labour of ₦1,800,000 and direct expenses of ₦400,000. If prime cost is 70% of production cost, what is the factory overhead
questions.explanation: Prime cost = ₦2.5m + ₦1.8m + ₦400k = ₦4.7m. Since prime cost is 70% of production cost, production cost = ₦4.7m ÷ 0.70 = ₦6.714m. Factory overhead = ₦6.714m − ₦4.7m = ₦2.014m. None of the options matches. DO NOT USE.

questions.text: A partner is entitled to 10% interest on capital of ₦800,000. If the partnership makes a profit of ₦600,000 before interest, what is the interest on capital
questions.explanation: Interest = 10% × ₦800,000 = ₦80,000. This is an appropriation of profit, not an expense.

questions.text: A club has the following information: Cash received from members ₦750,000; Rent paid ₦120,000; Electricity paid ₦85,000; Purchase of equipment ₦200,000; Depreciation of equipment ₦40,000. What amount would appear in the receipts and payments account
questions.explanation: Receipts and payments account records actual cash transactions: ₦750,000 + ₦120,000 + ₦85,000 + ₦200,000 = ₦1,155,000 (cash payments). Depreciation is not included as it is non-cash. The correct option is the total cash payments.

questions.text: A company issues debentures of ₦5,000,000 at a discount of 8%. The amount received is
questions.explanation: Discount = 8% × ₦5m = ₦400,000. Amount received = ₦5m − ₦400k = ₦4.6m.

questions.text: A trader's mark-up is 40% on cost. If the selling price is ₦2,800,000, what is the cost
questions.explanation: Selling price = 140% of cost. Cost = ₦2.8m ÷ 1.40 = ₦2m.

questions.text: A business has cost of sales of ₦6,400,000. If the gross profit margin is 20%, what are the sales
questions.explanation: If gross profit margin is 20%, then cost of sales is 80% of sales. Sales = ₦6.4m ÷ 0.80 = ₦8m.

questions.text: A partnership has assets of ₦7,800,000 and liabilities of ₦2,200,000. If partners' capital accounts show ₦4,000,000, what is the balance on the current accounts
questions.explanation: Total capital = Assets − Liabilities = ₦7.8m − ₦2.2m = ₦5.6m. Current account balances = ₦5.6m − ₦4m = ₦1.6m.

questions.text: A non-profit organization has an accumulated fund of ₦3,200,000 at the beginning of the year. During the year, income was ₦900,000 and expenditure was ₦750,000. What is the closing accumulated fund
questions.explanation: Surplus = ₦900k − ₦750k = ₦150k. Closing accumulated fund = ₦3.2m + ₦150k = ₦3.35m.

questions.explanation: Cost of sales = ₦2m + ₦8.5m + ₦400k − ₦1.8m = ₦9.1m.

questions.text: A trader sells goods at a markup of 30% on cost. If the cost is ₦2,000,000, the selling price is
questions.explanation: Selling price = ₦2m × 130% = ₦2.6m.

questions.text: A customer owing ₦3,000,000 is allowed a cash discount of 3% for prompt payment. The amount received is
questions.explanation: Discount = 3% × ₦3m = ₦90,000. Amount received = ₦3m − ₦90k = ₦2.91m.

questions.text: A debit note is issued by a buyer to a supplier to
options: Reduce the amount owed to the supplier
Increase the amount owed to the supplier
questions.explanation: A debit note notifies the supplier of goods returned, increasing the amount owed to the buyer or reducing the amount owed to the supplier.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦15,000,000 and a gross profit margin of 40%. The cost of sales is
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 40% × ₦15m = ₦6m. Cost of sales = ₦15m − ₦6m = ₦9m.

questions.text: The error in which a transaction is recorded in the wrong class of account is an
questions.explanation: An error of principle occurs when the correct amount is posted to the wrong type of account.

questions.text: A suspense account has a credit balance of ₦60,000. It is discovered that a receipt of ₦80,000 from a customer was correctly entered in the cash book but credited to the customer's account as ₦20,000. The correcting entry is
questions.explanation: The customer's account was credited with ₦20,000 instead of ₦80,000 — a short credit of ₦60,000. To correct this, the customer's account is credited with ₦60,000, and suspense is debited.

questions.text: A bank statement shows a credit balance of ₦3,000,000. Unpresented cheques are ₦450,000 and uncredited lodgements are ₦300,000. The cash-book balance is
questions.explanation: Cash book balance = ₦3m − ₦450k + ₦300k = ₦2.85m.

questions.text: A bank charge of ₦25,000 appears on the bank statement but not in the cash book. Before preparing the bank reconciliation, the cash book should be
questions.explanation: Bank charges reduce the bank balance, so the bank column of the cash book is credited.

questions.text: A petty cashier operates on an imprest of ₦250,000. During the period, expenses total ₦186,400. The reimbursement amount is
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system, reimbursement equals the amount spent: ₦186,400.

questions.text: A non-current asset was purchased for ₦6,000,000. It has a useful life of 6 years and a residual value of ₦600,000. Using the straight-line method, the net book value after 3 years is
questions.explanation: Annual depreciation = (₦6m − ₦600k) ÷ 6 = ₦900,000. After 3 years, accumulated depreciation = ₦2.7m. NBV = ₦6m − ₦2.7m = ₦3.3m.

questions.text: A business has current assets of ₦9,600,000 and current liabilities of ₦3,200,000. The current ratio is
questions.explanation: Current ratio = ₦9.6m ÷ ₦3.2m = 3:1.

questions.text: A business has current assets of ₦7,200,000, inventory of ₦2,400,000 and current liabilities of ₦2,400,000. The acid-test ratio is
questions.explanation: Quick assets = ₦7.2m − ₦2.4m = ₦4.8m. Acid-test ratio = ₦4.8m ÷ ₦2.4m = 2:1.

questions.text: A business has cost of sales of ₦12,000,000 and average inventory of ₦2,000,000. The stock turnover is
questions.explanation: Stock turnover = ₦12m ÷ ₦2m = 6 times.

questions.text: A company has 5,000,000 ordinary shares of ₦0.50 each. If the company declares a dividend of 8%, the dividend payable is
questions.explanation: Total nominal value = 5m × ₦0.50 = ₦2.5m. Dividend = 8% × ₦2.5m = ₦200,000.

questions.text: A manufacturing business has prime cost of ₦6,000,000 and factory overhead of ₦2,000,000. Opening work-in-progress was ₦500,000 and closing WIP was ₦700,000. The production cost is
questions.explanation: Production cost = Prime cost + Factory overhead + Opening WIP − Closing WIP = ₦6m + ₦2m + ₦500k − ₦700k = ₦7.8m.

questions.text: A trader has opening inventory of ₦1,000,000, purchases of ₦5,000,000 and closing inventory of ₦800,000. If the mark-up is 30%, the sales are
questions.explanation: Cost of sales = ₦1m + ₦5m − ₦800k = ₦5.2m. Sales = ₦5.2m × 130% = ₦6.76m. None of the options matches exactly. DO NOT USE.

questions.text: A business has credit sales of ₦24,000,000. Opening receivables were ₦3,000,000 and closing receivables were ₦4,000,000. The receivables turnover is
questions.explanation: Average receivables = (₦3m + ₦4m) ÷ 2 = ₦3.5m. Receivables turnover = ₦24m ÷ ₦3.5m = 6.86 times.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦18,000,000 and a gross profit margin of 35%. What is the gross profit
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 35% × ₦18m = ₦6.3m.

questions.text: A company has issued share capital of ₦12,000,000. If the company repurchases ₦3,000,000 worth of shares, the issued share capital becomes
questions.explanation: Issued share capital = ₦12m − ₦3m = ₦9m.

questions.text: A partner is entitled to 10% interest on capital of ₦2,000,000. The interest on capital is

A non-profit organization has subscriptions received in advance of ₦200,000 at the beginning and ₦150,000 at the end. Subscriptions outstanding were ₦180,000 at the beginning and ₦250,000 at the end. If cash received is ₦4,000,000, the subscription income is
questions.explanation: Income = Cash + closing arrears − opening arrears + opening advance − closing advance = ₦4m + ₦250k − ₦180k + ₦200k − ₦150k = ₦4.12m.

questions.text: A club has an accumulated fund of ₦2,000,000. During the year, the club had income of ₦1,200,000 and expenditure of ₦1,400,000. The closing accumulated fund is
questions.explanation: Deficit = ₦1.4m − ₦1.2m = ₦200k. Closing accumulated fund = ₦2m − ₦200k = ₦1.8m.

questions.text: A company issues 3,000,000 ordinary shares at ₦2.50 each. The nominal value is ₦1.50. The total amount credited to share premium is
questions.explanation: Premium per share = ₦2.50 − ₦1.50 = ₦1.00. Total premium = ₦1.00 × 3,000,000 = ₦3m.

questions.text: A manufacturing business has direct materials of ₦5,000,000, direct labour of ₦3,000,000 and factory overhead of ₦2,000,000. The prime cost is
questions.explanation: Prime cost = Direct materials + Direct labour = ₦5m + ₦3m = ₦8m.

questions.text: A trader's mark-up is 25% on cost. If the selling price is ₦5,000,000, the cost is
questions.explanation: Selling price = 125% of cost. Cost = ₦5m ÷ 1.25 = ₦4m.

questions.text: A business has cost of sales of ₦8,400,000 and a gross profit margin of 30%. The sales are
questions.explanation: If margin is 30%, cost is 70% of sales. Sales = ₦8.4m ÷ 0.70 = ₦12m.

questions.text: A business has a current ratio of 2.2:1 and current liabilities of ₦5,000,000. The current assets are
questions.explanation: Current assets = 2.2 × ₦5m = ₦11m.

questions.text: A non-current asset costing ₦8,000,000 has accumulated depreciation of ₦3,200,000. If it is sold for ₦4,200,000, the result is
questions.explanation: Net book value = ₦8m − ₦3.2m = ₦4.8m. Loss on sale = ₦4.8m − ₦4.2m = ₦600,000.

questions.text: A trader's gross profit is ₦5,400,000. If the gross profit margin is 45%, the sales are
questions.explanation: Sales = Gross profit ÷ Margin = ₦5.4m ÷ 0.45 = ₦12m.

questions.text: A business has current assets of ₦14,000,000, inventory of ₦4,000,000 and current liabilities of ₦5,000,000. The acid-test ratio is
questions.explanation: Quick assets = ₦14m − ₦4m = ₦10m. Acid-test ratio = ₦10m ÷ ₦5m = 2:1.

questions.text: The accounting concept that requires that financial statements should not be misleading is the
questions.explanation: The fair presentation concept requires that financial statements present information honestly and without misleading users.

questions.text: A business has sales of ₦20,000,000 and a gross profit margin of 30%. If operating expenses are ₦3,000,000, the operating profit is
questions.explanation: Gross profit = 30% × ₦20m = ₦6m. Operating profit = ₦6m − ₦3m = ₦3m.

questions.text: A company issues 4,000,000 ordinary shares at ₦3.00 each. The nominal value is ₦2.00. The total amount received is
questions.explanation: Total received = 4,000,000 × ₦3.00 = ₦12m.

questions.text: A business has assets of ₦30,000,000 and liabilities of ₦11,500,000. If the owner withdraws ₦800,000 and introduces ₦1,200,000, what is the new capital
questions.explanation: Initial capital = ₦30m − ₦11.5m = ₦18.5m. New capital = ₦18.5m − ₦800k + ₦1.2m = ₦18.9m.

questions.text: The accounting principle that requires that expenses should be recognized in the same period as the revenue they helped to generate is the
questions.explanation: The matching concept requires that expenses be matched with the revenue they generate in the same accounting period to determine accurate profit.

questions.text: A business has current assets of ₦8,400,000 and current liabilities of ₦2,800,000. It purchases inventory worth ₦1,200,000 on credit. What is the new current ratio
questions.explanation: New current assets = ₦8.4m + ₦1.2m = ₦9.6m. New current liabilities = ₦2.8m + ₦1.2m = ₦4.0m. New current ratio = ₦9.6m ÷ ₦4.0m = 2.4:1.

questions.text: The accounting concept that assumes a business will continue to operate indefinitely is the
questions.explanation: The going concern concept assumes that the business will continue to operate for the foreseeable future, justifying the use of historical cost for assets.

questions.text: A machine costing ₦12,000,000 has an estimated useful life of 8 years and a residual value of ₦1,200,000. Using the straight-line method, what is the accumulated depreciation after 5 years
questions.explanation: Annual depreciation = (₦12m − ₦1.2m) ÷ 8 = ₦10.8m ÷ 8 = ₦1.35m. Accumulated depreciation after 5 years = ₦1.35m × 5 = ₦6.75m.

questions.text: The accounting principle that requires that similar items should be treated in the same way from one period to the next is the
questions.explanation: The consistency concept requires that the same accounting methods and principles should be used from one accounting period to another to allow meaningful comparison of financial statements.
